title: Influence of Laser Wavelength and Pulse Energy on Composition in the APT Analysis of Proton and Heavy-Ion Irradiated GaN
content: A wide range of systems, from civilian to military, government to private industry increasingly rely on electronic components to operate in high energy irradiation environments. Applications include space and nuclear devices, where electronic devices must function despite being subject to gamma, neutron, and/or heavy ion bombardment. Traditional Si based transistors and other In based materials have relatively low lattice displacement energies (7-13 eV), making them highly susceptible to point defects. In contrast, GaN has a relatively high displacement energy (19 eV), making it a promising radiation-hard material [1]. However, the types of defects generated by various irradiating species is largely unknown for GaN materials and must be characterized at atomic to near-atomic levels to understand the limitations of any devices incorporating GaN.
